Alright, let’s break down Trump Derangement Syndrome (TDS) like it’s a tragicomic medical condition, complete with stages—because nothing says “healthy coping mechanism” like turning political obsession into a mock disease progression. Here we go:

Stage 1: The Triggering (Pre-Diagnosis) Symptoms: Mild irritation at the sight of a red hat, spontaneous eye-rolls when someone says “MAGA,” and an inexplicable urge to fact-check a tweet that doesn’t even exist anymore. Comedic Prognosis: At this point, you’re still functional. You might mutter “orange man bad” under your breath at a family barbecue, but you can still enjoy the potato salad. Friends notice you’re a little snippy during election season, but they chalk it up to too much coffee—or not enough. You’re not terminal yet; you’re just mildly allergic to golden hair and brash confidence.

Stage 2: The Hyperfixation (Early TDS) Symptoms: You’ve started doom-scrolling X for Trump-related content, arguing with strangers in the replies, and yelling “Covfefe was a cry for help!” at your bewildered dog. Your Google search history looks like a conspiracy board: “Trump tax returns,” “Trump golf swing analysis,” “Trump secretly a time traveler?” Comedic Prognosis: You’re in too deep to back out, but not so far gone that you’ve lost your sense of humor. You’re that guy at the party who turns “How’s the weather?” into a 20-minute rant about hush money payments. Your friends still invite you out, but they’ve started hiding the news apps on your phone.

Stage 3: The Meltdown (Moderate TDS) Symptoms: Full-on physical reactions—shrieking at TV screens, throwing popcorn at debate reruns, and writing manifestos in ALL CAPS about how “HE’S RUINING EVERYTHING.” You’ve begun seeing Trump in unrelated places: the shape of your toast, the clouds, your boss’s comb-over. Comedic Prognosis: This is peak comedy gold for everyone except you. Your family’s staging an intervention, but you’re too busy accusing the goldfish of being a Russian asset. You’re one step away from wearing a tinfoil hat, but you still manage to pay your bills—barely.

Stage 4: The Evangelist (Advanced TDS) Symptoms: You’re now a prophet of the anti-Trump apocalypse, preaching to anyone who’ll listen (and many who won’t). You’ve got binders of “evidence” and a podcast called “The Art of the Squeal.” Your vocabulary is 90% buzzwords: “fascist,” “grifter,” “insurrection.” Sleep is a distant memory; you’re sustained by rage and Starbucks. Comedic Prognosis: You’ve become a caricature of yourself, and it’s hilarious to watch—unless you’re the barista who has to hear about Mar-a-Lago’s zoning violations for the fifth time this week. Your loved ones have given up; they just nod and hand you a megaphone to get it over with.

Stage 5: Terminal TDS (The Point of No Return) Symptoms: Total detachment from reality. You’re convinced Trump is personally responsible for your Wi-Fi dropping, the neighbor’s loud dog, and the fact that your favorite cereal got discontinued. You’ve moved into a bunker, surrounded by screenshots of old tweets, muttering “I knew it” to no one. Comedic Prognosis: At this stage, you’re a living sitcom no one can turn off. You’ve transcended politics into performance art. Friends stop by to check on you, but they leave with popcorn and a story for the group chat. Recovery? Unlikely. You’re in a love-hate marriage with the man, and he doesn’t even know your name.

So there you have it—Trump Derangement Syndrome, from a twitchy eyebrow to a full-blown bunker meltdown. The only cure? Maybe a good laugh and a social media detox… but good luck with that!
